EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the classic pattern of a single alkoxy-substituted benzene.  
• 1003 cm⁻¹ (very strong) is the A₁g ring-breathing mode of a monosubstituted benzene; this band shifts or weakens in para-disubstituted rings, so candidates with two ring substituents are disfavoured.  
• 741 cm⁻¹ (strong) matches the C-H out-of-plane bend typical for monosubstituted rings.  
• 1255 cm⁻¹ (strong) is the C–O stretching band of an aromatic-alkoxy group; the accompanying weaker C–O–C mode at 1171 cm⁻¹ supports an alkoxy substituent.  
• 1593 and 1614 cm⁻¹ are the expected aromatic C=C stretches; 2923/2879 cm⁻¹ are aliphatic C–H and 3057 cm⁻¹ is aromatic C–H, fitting an alkyl–O–phenyl structure.  
Among the candidates, molecule 6 (CCOc1ccccc1, phenetole) is the only monosubstituted benzene that contains an alkoxy group, matching all key bands, whereas candidates with two ring substituents or no O–alkyl group fail to account for the 1255 cm⁻¹ feature or would shift the 1003 cm⁻¹ ring-breathing band.
